title: The Yearbook of the water tower
premise: Theo Joubert, a meticulous statistician for the Millbrook High basketball team, has spent two decades keeping their head down after a childhood incident taught them that visibility is dangerous. When they find coded directions hidden in their late grandmother's recipe box, they uncover her role in a decades-old cover-up orchestrated by the town's most powerful family — one that destroyed Theo's own family's name. As Theo deciphers the evidence, they realize winning the state championship is the only way to force the town to listen, because the anniversary ceremony where the truth can be exposed happens the same night as the final game. In the end, Theo trades their hard-won invisibility for justice, exposing the corruption at the cost of the quiet life they built, but reclaiming the memory and dignity of everyone the water tower's shadow erased.
about_author: Sebastian Oyelaran is a former small-town sports reporter who spent years covering Friday night games in towns where everyone knew which families mattered. He writes young adult fiction about ordinary kids who discover the machinery underneath their hometowns.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Numbers
chapters.summary: Theo Joubert, team statistician, catalogs every game with obsessive precision while staying deliberately invisible at Millbrook High. A flashback hints at why: a childhood incident involving the Delacroix family. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness — safety purchased with silence.

chapters.title: Grandma's Cardamom Lie
chapters.summary: Clearing out his grandmother Ruth's kitchen after her funeral, Theo finds a recipe card titled 'Preserves' containing coordinates, dates, and initials instead of ingredients. POV shifts between Theo's present grief and confusion. The beat is destabilization: the careful world begins to crack.

chapters.title: What the Tower Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo investigates the water tower from the recipe card, finding a rusted maintenance hatch and scratched initials matching his grandfather's. His best friend Priya notices his distraction. The beat is dread mixed with the first thrill of purpose.

chapters.title: The Delacroix Doctrine
chapters.summary: Research reveals Judge Ambrose Delacroix — patriarch of the town's founding family — presided over every major ruling for forty years, including the 1985 case that ruined Theo's grandfather's business. The beat is cold anger as patterns emerge in the numbers.

chapters.title: Tryouts and Trapdoors
chapters.summary: Basketball season opens; Coach Brandt, a Delacroix ally, benches Theo's friend Marcus unfairly. Theo notices the scoring rotations are manipulated to favor Delacroix-sponsored players. The beat is the personal becoming political — the rigging isn't just history.

chapters.title: Recipe for Ruin
chapters.summary: Deciphering more cards, Theo learns Ruth documented Delacroix's bribery scheme — land deals buried under eminent domain rulings — and hid the evidence inside the tower before she was scared into silence. The beat is awe at grandma's courage and fury at her fear.

chapters.title: Priya Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Priya catches Theo breaking into the tower archives and demands the truth. Instead of turning him in, she offers her hacking skills. The beat is reluctant trust — Theo's first act of visibility in twenty years is letting someone in.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts
chapters.summary: Judge Delacroix's grandson Julian, the team's star player, confronts Theo about 'snooping,' revealing the family knows someone is asking questions. The beat is menace wrapped in charm; power smiles before it bites.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Careful
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: Theo visits his mother, who still flinches at the Delacroix name, and understands his invisibility was inherited trauma. He decides the pattern ends with him. The beat is grief transforming into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Rafters
chapters.summary: Theo and Priya retrieve a waterlogged ledger from the tower — names, payments, signatures, including the current mayor and coach. But a motion sensor trips; someone knows they were there. The beat is triumph curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: Marcus is suspended on fabricated charges, and Theo realizes it's retaliation meant to break the team before playoffs. Coach Brandt delivers a veiled threat. The beat is injustice made intimate and immediate.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Theo maps the season: winning states forces the town into the spotlight, guaranteeing press coverage on the exact night of the tower's centennial ceremony — when Delacroix will be honored. The plan crystallizes. The beat is strategic hope.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks Ruth's house; the remaining recipe cards are gone. Theo realizes he kept copies in the one place no one looks — his statistics notebooks. The beat is violation, then grim relief: the numbers survive.

chapters.title: Julian's Cracks
chapters.summary: Julian, pressured by his grandfather, hesitates before a dirty play and nearly apologizes to Marcus. A private scene shows Julian drowning in inherited guilt. The beat is the enemy revealed as another prisoner of the family name.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Delacroix summons Theo: full scholarship money, Marcus reinstated, his mother's debts cleared — if the ledger disappears. For the first time, Theo sees the price of silence itemized. The beat is temptation rendered almost reasonable.

chapters.title: What Grandma Would Do
chapters.summary: Theo finds Ruth's final unsent letter: an apology for staying silent, addressed to him. He refuses the deal publicly enough that Delacroix knows refusal means war. The beat is inheritance reclaimed — courage passed down like a recipe.

chapters.title: Playoffs: Every Possession
chapters.summary: The semifinal against Delacroix-funded rival Crestwood. Marcus returns; the rigged rotations fail against Theo's counter-strategy fed from the bench. They win by two. The beat is collective defiance — the team becomes the movement.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Priya discovers Delacroix plans to have the tower demolished Sunday morning, destroying the physical evidence chain. The final game and the centennial ceremony are tomorrow — everything converges on one night. The beat is breathless compression.

chapters.title: The Final That Matters
chapters.summary: Championship night. The gym is packed, press present, Delacroix honored at halftime. Theo plays the game of his life as statistician-turned-strategist while Priya prepares the reveal. The beat is sustained adrenaline — two championships running in parallel.

chapters.title: Buzzer
chapters.summary: Millbrook wins on a last-second play Theo designed. At the ceremony, as Delacroix accepts his honor, the scoreboard screen switches to the ledger scans. The crowd reads their own names. The beat is catharsis — the whistle blown from inside the game.

chapters.title: After the Whistle
chapters.summary: Fallout: investigations open, Brandt resigns, Julian testifies against his grandfather. Theo's mother weeps at the front page bearing her father's cleared name. The beat is bittersweet vindication — justice arrived, but nothing returns to what it was.

chapters.title: The New Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Months later, Theo adds his own card to Ruth's box — not hiding it, but keeping it, a record of what memory costs and what it's worth. He walks through town visible, greeted by name. The beat is quiet arrival: invisibility traded for belonging.
